beats.label: S1 · Revenge, then nothing
beats.text: Frank finishes off the gangs who killed his family and vanishes into demolition work, waking at 3 AM to the same nightmare with no war left to fight.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes Frank's post-revenge emptiness — the vacuum a new mission has to fill.

beats.label: S1 · Micro and the tape
beats.text: A hacker calling himself Micro contacts Frank with proof: his family was murdered to bury a leaked video of his Marine unit torturing an Afghan officer in Kandahar.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reframe of the pilot — the family killings were a cover-up, not a mob hit.

beats.label: S1 · The unlikely alliance
beats.text: Frank corners Micro — NSA analyst David Lieberman, presumed dead after leaking the tape — and the two ally to hunt down 'Agent Orange', the CIA man who ran the black op.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's engine: Frank + Lieberman targeting the conspiracy behind Cerberus.

beats.label: S1 · Russo, the mole
beats.text: DHS agent Dinah Madani chases the same conspiracy, using Frank's Marine best friend Billy Russo as her source — not knowing Russo is Agent Orange's man on the inside.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the double betrayal that drives the last act and all of season 2.

beats.label: S1 · Outed
beats.text: Traumatised veteran Lewis Wilson starts bombing New York; Frank is caught on camera at the scene and outed to the world as alive and a suspected terrorist.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ends Frank's ghost status — every remaining move happens under manhunt pressure.

beats.label: S1 · Rawlins killed, Russo turns
beats.text: Frank kills Agent Orange — CIA officer William Rawlins — at the power station, but Russo, exposed as complicit, turns on Frank and is only stopped when Madani arrives.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Frank finally knows Russo betrayed him; the personal war replaces the conspiracy war.

beats.label: S1 · The carousel
beats.text: At the carousel where his family died, Frank refuses to kill Russo and instead mangles his face; Russo shoots Madani in the head, but all three survive.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Every principal of season 2 is left alive and permanently marked by this night.

cliffhanger.text: Frank has been officially cleared and his family avenged, but he tells Curtis's support group that he's scared of who he is without a war. Russo lives — disfigured, publicly blamed for everything — and Madani has recovered from a bullet to the head knowing exactly who put it there.
questions: What does Frank become when there is no one left to punish?
How does Russo, unmasked and disfigured, come back at the man who did it?
Will Madani stay in DHS after being made the fall guy for a CIA cover-up?

characters.name: Frank Castle
characters.line: Marine veteran and vigilante known as the Punisher; family avenged, name officially cleared, and now adrift with no mission left.

characters.name: Billy Russo
characters.line: Frank's Marine best friend turned traitor, exposed as Rawlins's enforcer; hospitalised, permanently disfigured, and publicly blamed for the whole conspiracy.

characters.name: Dinah Madani
characters.line: DHS agent who unravelled the Cerberus cover-up; shot in the head by Russo at the carousel and now recovering, having quietly let Frank walk free.

characters.name: David Lieberman
characters.line: Ex-NSA analyst 'Micro' who leaked the Kandahar tape; officially dead to the world, quietly reunited with his family, off the board.

characters.name: Curtis Hoyle
characters.line: Frank's ex-Marine friend and the one civilian tether he still trusts; runs a support group for veterans and has stood by him through everything.

beats.label: S2 · A girl in the bar
beats.text: In Michigan, Frank saves teen grifter 'Amy' from a squad of killers hunting her over photographs she took at a funeral, dragging her into his flight south.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The new mission that pulls Frank back into the fight and gives him someone to protect.

beats.label: S2 · Pilgrim, and back to New York
beats.text: The killers' leader — a devout enforcer named John Pilgrim — assaults an Ohio sheriff's station to reach them; Madani flies in and pulls Frank and Amy back to New York.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the season's second antagonist and folds Amy's plot into the returning New York cast.

beats.label: S2 · Russo walks out
beats.text: In New York, Billy Russo escapes his hospital guards with the help of his therapist Krista Dumont, claiming amnesia about everything he did to Frank.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's other engine goes live — Russo is loose, and Dumont is his new protector.

beats.label: S2 · Who Pilgrim works for
beats.text: Amy's photographs show closeted Senator David Schultz kissing another man; his wealthy religious parents are the ones paying Pilgrim to kill anyone who's seen them.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's real villains and makes the Amy plot a war against a specific family, not a mystery.

beats.label: S2 · Russo builds a gang
beats.text: Russo recruits struggling veterans from Curtis's support group into a robbery crew and starts a relationship with Dumont, who becomes his shelter and enabler.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns Russo from a fugitive into an army, and locks Dumont in as his co-conspirator, not his doctor.

beats.label: S2 · The Valhalla trap
beats.text: On Dumont's coaching, Russo lures Frank into a warehouse trap where he stands over three innocent women executed by Russo's crew, staged to break his sense of righteousness.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's cruellest move — the point where Russo goes from betrayer to something Frank must actually destroy.

beats.label: S2 · The Punisher, for good
beats.text: Frank kills a dying Russo, spares Pilgrim for his sons' sake, blackmails the Schultzes into ruin, and refuses Madani's CIA offer — embracing the Punisher mantle for good.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes both antagonists and settles Frank's identity question from S1 in the opposite direction: no normal life.

cliffhanger.text: Three months on, Frank is operating openly as the Punisher and has turned down every path back to a normal life. Russo is dead, the Schultzes are ruined, Amy is starting over in Florida with their money, and Madani has been promoted to a CIA that would very much like to point Frank somewhere useful.
questions: Now that revenge and conspiracy are both settled, what mission does Frank invent for himself?
Does Madani's new CIA role mean she'll keep trying to pull him into sanctioned work?
Can Pilgrim, spared and grieving, actually raise his two sons in peace?

characters.name: Frank Castle
characters.line: Has stopped hiding from the name; operating openly as the Punisher and refusing every offer of a life outside the war.

characters.name: Billy Russo
characters.line: Dead — killed by Frank at Curtis's support-group site after his robbery crew fell apart and he crawled there for help.

characters.name: Dinah Madani
characters.line: Recovered from the carousel shooting and now working for the CIA under Marion James; still the closest thing Frank has to a friend in law enforcement.

characters.name: Amy Bendix
characters.line: The teen grifter Frank protected all season; smart and mouthy, sent to Florida with enough Schultz money to build a real life.

characters.name: Curtis Hoyle
characters.line: Frank's ex-Marine friend; nearly killed by Pilgrim and betrayed by veterans from his own support group, but still running it.

characters.name: John Pilgrim
characters.line: The Schultzes' religious enforcer; his wife dead, his employers destroyed, spared by Frank on the condition he goes home to his two sons.

characters.name: Krista Dumont
characters.line: Russo's therapist turned lover and strategist; survived a fall from her apartment window pushed by Madani, and is exposed as his accomplice.
